editorial.headline: Air-Conditioning and Ventilation, Defined
editorial.standfirst: This building-systems activity is nationally open to PMA at up to full foreign ownership; in Bali it is not blocked by the province’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Air-conditioning and ventilation installation sounds narrower than it is. This activity is the on-site installation and maintenance of ventilation and air-conditioning systems in both residential and non-residential buildings. Its practical terrain includes the connective work that makes those systems operate: piping, ducting and sheet-metal work. The focus is therefore not simply the supply of equipment, but the built-environment work of putting ventilation and cooling systems into place and keeping them maintained. It is an activity rooted in the physical systems of a building, whether the building is a home or serves another purpose.

That definition gives the code a clear professional centre of gravity. It speaks to firms whose work is organised around building systems: executing installation work and then maintaining the ventilation or air-conditioning components already in service. The recorded scale access is broad, covering Micro, Small, Medium and Large enterprises. The same activity can therefore be registered at each stated business scale. That matters because a business may be assessed here for the defined installation and maintenance work itself, rather than through a vague catch-all description. In practical terms, piping, ducting and sheet metal belong inside the stated scope when they form part of the ventilation and cooling work.

On foreign participation, the national position is direct. The activity is marked open to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That is a full national foreign-ownership ceiling, rather than a partial stake limit. The legal source listed for that position is Presidential Regulation No. 10 of 2021 and No. 49 of 2021. For a founder assessing the activity at national level, these fields establish the essential point: this is a foreign-open installation-and-maintenance business category, available at each of the four stated enterprise scales. The ownership position and the scale access are presented separately, but they meet in the same recorded activity.

Bali needs to be read on its own terms. The province’s standing rule blocks PMA across all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. This activity, however, is not recorded as blocked by that moratorium. At the Large scale, its OSS risk is recorded as Medium-High/High, which is why the record says the moratorium does not block it. The Bali status is OK or Higher Risk: not a moratorium bar for PMA registration on the facts given here. The distinction is important. National openness is not being overridden by the Bali rule in this record, and the risk language remains part of the Bali picture.
